name: Omarchy Broadcast
author: Raul Dias
description: Status and control of the omarchy-broadcastd virtual camera in the Omarchy bar: on/off, camera selection, the background effect and the video effects' settings as the daemon's modules offer them, the camera's own settings as the daemon publishes them (image, white balance, exposure, focus and zoom), a background gallery (pick a bundled background or add your own image), an away image shown when the camera is off or an effect cannot run, a live preview, live stream figures, the Omarchy Broadcast Mic (its noise and echo processing as the daemon's audio modules offer it, its input device, the default-microphone choice, and an indicator while apps record from it), and a setup dialog for the effect modules, their order and backends, the daemon's configuration, your backgrounds and diagnostics. Effects need omarchy-broadcastd 0.24.0, the configuration in the setup dialog 0.25.0, the microphone D-Bus API revision 13, the background gallery revision 15, the away image revision 17.

barWidget.description: Shows the virtual camera's state, and a microphone glyph while apps record from the Omarchy Broadcast Mic; left click opens the panel with the live preview, effects, cameras, the microphone and status, middle click turns the camera on or off, right click opens the setup dialog (modules, stage order, backends, daemon configuration, diagnostics).

schema.label: omarchy-broadcast CLI path
schema.description: Optional. Absolute path to the omarchy-broadcast binary (a leading ~/ is your home); a bare name or a relative path is refused. Empty: omarchy-broadcast on PATH.

schema.label: Preview in the panel
schema.description: On: opening the panel starts the camera and shows what apps receive. Off: the panel shows the preview only while another app already uses the camera. Needs omarchy-broadcast 0.18 or newer.

schema.label: Preview rate
schema.description: 15 or 30 frames per second; any other value reads as 15.

schema.label: Panel tab
schema.description: The tab the panel shows under the preview; the panel remembers the last one chosen. Any other value reads as effect.
